## Proof

We work in $\operatorname{Spec} A$ equipped with the Zariski topology. Recall that the closed subsets of $\operatorname{Spec} A$ are precisely the sets
$$V(I) = \{\mathfrak q \in \operatorname{Spec} A : I \subseteq \mathfrak q\},$$
where $I$ ranges over all ideals of $A$, and that arbitrary intersections of closed sets satisfy
$$\bigcap_{j \in J} V(I_j) = V\!\left(\sum_{j \in J} I_j\right).$$

The closure $\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}}$ of the singleton $\{\mathfrak p\}$ is, by definition, the smallest closed set containing $\mathfrak p$, i.e. the intersection of all closed sets containing $\mathfrak p$:
$$\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}} = \bigcap_{\mathfrak p \in V(I)} V(I).$$

Now $\mathfrak p \in V(I)$ holds if and only if $I \subseteq \mathfrak p$. Hence
$$\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}} = \bigcap_{I \subseteq \mathfrak p} V(I) = V\!\left(\sum_{I \subseteq \mathfrak p} I\right).$$

Consider the ideal $S := \sum_{I \subseteq \mathfrak p} I$.

- Since $\mathfrak p$ itself is an ideal with $\mathfrak p \subseteq \mathfrak p$, it appears among the summands, so $\mathfrak p \subseteq S$.
- Every summand $I$ satisfies $I \subseteq \mathfrak p$, so $S \subseteq \mathfrak p$.

Therefore $S = \mathfrak p$, and consequently
$$\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}} = V(\mathfrak p) = \{\mathfrak q \in \operatorname{Spec} A : \mathfrak p \subseteq \mathfrak q\},$$
which is exactly the set of all prime ideals containing $\mathfrak p$.

Thus the statement is **true**: the closure of $\{\mathfrak p\}$ in $\operatorname{Spec} A$ equals $V(\mathfrak p)$. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE

The problem asks to prove or disprove: The closure of {p} in Spec A equals V(p), the set of all prime ideals containing p.

Let me think about this carefully.

In Spec A with the Zariski topology, the closed sets are V(I) = {q ∈ Spec A : I ⊆ q} for ideals I.

The closure of a point p: closure of {p} is the smallest closed set containing p. A closed set containing p is V(I) where I ⊆ p. The smallest such closed set... we want the intersection of all V(I) containing p, i.e., V(I) with I ⊆ p. The largest such I is p itself (well, the ideal p). So closure of {p} = V(p).

Wait, let me be careful. V(I) contains p iff I ⊆ p. The closure of {p} = ∩{V(I) : p ∈ V(I)} = ∩{V(I) : I ⊆ p} = V(Σ I : I ⊆ p) = V(p) since the sum of all ideals contained in p is p itself (p is one of them, and all are contained in p, so the sum is contained in p, and contains p, so equals p).

So closure of {p} = V(p).

V(p) = {q ∈ Spec A : p ⊆ q} = set of prime ideals containing p.

So the statement is TRUE.

Let me write a clean proof.

Actually, let me double check the standard result. The closure of {p} is V(p) = {q : p ⊆ q}. Yes, this is the standard result. Points q in the closure of {p} are exactly those with p ⊆ q (specialization order). This is correct.

So the proof:

1. Closed sets in Spec A are exactly V(I) for ideals I.
2. closure({p}) = intersection of all closed sets containing {p}.
3. A closed set V(I) contains p iff I ⊆ p.
4. So closure({p}) = ∩_{I ⊆ p} V(I) = V(∑_{I ⊆ p} I) = V(p).

The key identity: ∩_{j} V(I_j) = V(∑ I_j). And ∑_{I ⊆ p} I = p because p is among the ideals contained in p (p ⊆ p), so the sum contains p; and every I in the sum is ⊆ p, so the sum ⊆ p. Hence sum = p.

Therefore closure({p}) = V(p). QED.
